title: Microsoft Dataverse: unlicensed Entra users as activity recipients
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents the recipient licence exemption, but does not establish that the feature is included in a named existing licence. The statement that the switch is portal-only also goes beyond the documentation; the briefing should describe the undocumented automation surface without asserting it cannot exist. The preview qualification and the security-role prerequisite also need clearer treatment.

The feature requires an administrator to opt in.
claims.quote: Turn on the Activities for users without licenses feature in the Power Platform admin center to allow any user in your tenant with a Microsoft Entra ID to be added to activity recipient fields

claims.claim: The feature is included in a licence the product already needs.
claims.quote: Searched: "add-unlicensed-users-activities" pricing included license charge; "Activities for users without licenses" pricing licensing cost. Opened the feature page; it exempts recipients but identifies no existing licence that includes the feature.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown. Keep the recipient licence exemption in licensing.notes, but do not treat that exemption as proof that the feature is included in a named existing licence. State in the cost rationale that overall feature licensing is not yet published.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Recipients do not need a Dataverse or Power Apps licence to be added through this feature.
claims.quote: Turn on this feature in the Power Platform admin center to allow users with a Microsoft Entra ID to be added to activity recipient fields without requiring a Dataverse or Power Apps license.

claims.claim: The feature allows active Microsoft Entra users in the tenant to be activity recipients in Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote:
Add users without licenses to activity recipient fields (preview)
Users without licenses are people in your tenant who have an active Microsoft Entra ID account but don't have a Dataverse or Power Apps license.
claims.fix: At the start of What's changing, explicitly say that Microsoft Learn currently documents this as a preview feature and that the described behaviour and recipient licensing apply to that preview. The roadmap phase list and a preview date alone do not qualify the documented behaviour.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Selecting an Entra user for an activity creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment.
claims.quote: When you select a Microsoft Entra ID user for an activity, Dataverse creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment so that the user can be added to the activity's recipient fields.

claims.claim: Assigning a licence later automatically updates the unlicensed user to a licensed user.

claims.claim: Earlier activities remain associated with the same user record after licence assignment.
claims.quote: Activities previously associated with the user remain associated with the same user record. No migration or conversion of the user or their existing activities is required.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature requires granting all users in the tenant read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.claim: The feature introduces no autonomous activity; record creation follows a user's recipient selection.
claims.quote: When you select a Microsoft Entra ID user for an activity, Dataverse creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment so that the user can be added to the activity's recipient fields.

claims.claim: The feature switch is configured per environment.
claims.quote:
In the Manage pane, select Environments. Then select an environment.
Select Settings.
Select Product, and then select Features.

claims.claim: The feature page requires Privileged Role Administrator for granting table read access.
claims.quote: You need to be a Privileged Role Administrator in the Microsoft Entra admin center to grant users read access to the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator turns on the feature.
claims.quote: You need to be a Power Platform administrator to turn on the feature in Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Existing security roles can be updated to grant read permission on the Entra ID table.
claims.quote: Update each existing security role assigned to users and add read permission for the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout
claims.claim: An alternative is to create a custom role with Entra ID table read permission and assign it to all users.
claims.quote: Create a custom security role that grants read permission for the Microsoft Entra ID table, and then assign the role to all users.

claims.claim: The documented path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Activities for users without licenses > Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... select Environments. Then select an environment. ... Select Settings. ... Select Product, and then select Features. ... Go to Activities for users without licenses. ... Select the Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields checkbox.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a feature-specific API or automation equivalent or identified the setting for the general CLI command.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" API PowerShell; Dataverse organization unlicensed activity recipients setting API EnableUnlicensed; organization reference "unlicensed" "activity". Opened feature and pac env references; no feature-specific call or setting identified.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a tenant-wide default control on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" "tenant-wide" default; "Activities for users without licenses" "tenant" "PowerShell" "API". Opened feature and pac env references; found environment selection but no tenant-wide default control.

claims.claim: The switch is portal-only.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" API organization setting tenant default pricing license; Dataverse organization unlicensed activity recipients setting API EnableUnlicensed. Opened feature and pac env references; neither states that only the portal can configure it.
claims.fix: Replace 'The switch is per environment and portal-only' with 'The switch is per environment. As of November 2026, Microsoft documents the admin UI but no feature-specific API or automation equivalent.' Keep controls[0].api null; undocumented automation does not establish a portal-only restriction.

claims.claim: pac env update-settings is a documented command for updating environment organization settings generally.
claims.quote: The pac env list-settings command returns all the columns from the first and only row of the organization entity type. Use pac env update-settings to change those settings.

claims.claim: No feature-specific charge has been published in the documentation found for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" "price" "charge"; "Activities for users without licenses" pricing licensing cost; "add-unlicensed-users-activities" pricing included license charge. Opened the feature page; no feature-specific charge or meter was stated.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist requires configuring Entra ID table read permission, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Plan the security role change: update existing roles or create a custom role with read on the Entra ID table.' Table rows: 'Whether unlicensed Entra users can be activity recipients'; 'Tenant-wide default for the feature'.
claims.fix: Add a controls row for 'Who can read the Microsoft Entra ID table', with the documented security-role prerequisite and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/add-unlicensed-users-activities#grant-users-read-access-to-the-microsoft-entra-id-table. Research the UI and API surfaces before filling them.
